hypotheses.hypothesis_title: Opening Inside Put/Call Wall Range Predicts Session Containment
hypotheses.verdict_reason: UNTESTABLE AS DEFINED: Wall width averages $35.93 (~7.3% of underlying), while the typical QQQ daily range is 1.5% and only 7 sessions in the test window had a range exceeding 3.7%. Close-based containment is structurally guaranteed (100% for both inside-open and outside-open groups) because a session would need to move ~$18 ($35.93/2) to breach one wall, which almost never occurs. The diff=0 does not mean walls have no effect — it means this metric cannot measure containment when walls are 5x the typical daily range. Lookahead note: walls use same-day EOD OI; the open is observed before that OI is final.

hypotheses.hypothesis_title: Opening Outside Put/Call Wall Range Predicts Same-Direction Continuation
hypotheses.verdict_reason: Rejection confirmed in the claimed direction: 0.0% continuation rate on 15 outside-wall opens (12 above call_wall, 3 below put_wall). All 15 outside-wall opens reversed back inside the wall by close — consistent with walls acting as mean-reversion boundaries, not breakout levels. N=15 is too small for statistical inference (binomial p=1.0000 is misleading for a one-sided test at the claimed threshold; the data goes opposite to the claim). Lookahead note: walls use same-day EOD OI; the open classification may be slightly contaminated. p_binomial is one-sided (alternative: rate > 50%).

hypotheses.hypothesis_title: Rising Price With Rising Open Interest Predicts Next-Session Continuation
hypotheses.verdict_reason: Rejected: rising OI on up days predicts WORSE next-session returns, opposite to hypothesis claim. mean_next_rising=-0.00110 vs mean_next_falling=+0.00137 (diff=-0.00248, Cliff's d=-0.158). Mann-Whitney p=0.9248 (one-sided, alternative: rising > falling) — strongly inconsistent with the claimed direction. Two-sided p ≈ 0.15 (inconclusive for the reverse claim). Methodological note: total_oi includes 0DTE contracts (created and expired same day in QQQ), making oi_change a noisy proxy for multi-day institutional positioning. The result may reflect 0DTE turnover patterns rather than persistent positioning.

hypotheses.hypothesis_title: Expiry Fridays Close Nearer Max Pain Than Opening Price
hypotheses.verdict_reason: Rejected (corrected test — Friday filter applied): win_rate=40.5%% on 37 expiry Fridays (n=37, wins=15, p_binomial=0.9061 one-sided). Price moves AWAY from max pain more often than toward it. Mean dist: open=8.794 -> close=10.161 (improvement=-1.367). No max-pain magnetism on weekly expiry Fridays. BUG FIX NOTE: Prior run used n=190 (all sessions) because QQQ has 0DTE options every day; has_expiry=True for all 190 dates. Corrected to filter dayofweek==4 (Fridays only).

hypotheses.hypothesis_title: Overnight Wall Shifts in the Same Direction Predict Next-Session Return Direction
hypotheses.verdict_reason: Rejected: no directional signal in claimed direction. mean_return_both_up=-0.00105 vs mean_down=-0.00053 (diff=-0.00052, Cliff's d=-0.030). Mann-Whitney p=0.5612 (one-sided, alternative: both_up > both_down). Two-sided p ≈ 0.88. N is critically small: n_both_up=20, n_both_down=10. Counter-intuitive pattern: win_rate_both_down=70% (7/10) vs win_rate_both_up=45% (9/20) — walls shifting down may weakly predict positive next-session return, opposite to hypothesis. N=10 is insufficient to conclude anything about the reverse direction.
